source.title: Training large language models on narrow tasks can lead to broad misalignment
source.authors: Jan Betley; Daniel Tan; Niels Warncke; Anna Sztyber-Betley; Xuchan Bao; Mart'in Soto; Megha Srivastava; Nathan Labenz; Owain Evans

record.file_problem: No evident garbling or truncation; the text includes the main paper and appendices through the final base-model examples.
record.tranche_reason: This is the original study: it fine-tunes models on insecure code and measures free-form misaligned answers on unrelated questions, with secure and educational-insecure controls.
record.gate_note: Rows record free-form misalignment results and the number-sequence experiment. The paper also reports deception, benchmark, capability, and code-generation results; those are not recorded as rows because they do not measure the claim versions’ specified free-form misalignment outcome. Results cited from other studies are excluded.
record.test_reason: This is the original source of the claim. It fine-tunes GPT-4o and open models on insecure code written for an unsuspecting user and measures misaligned free-form answers on unrelated questions. It compares these with secure, educational-insecure and jailbroken controls, and adds evil-number, in-context, data-diversity, training-dynamics and base-model experiments. Because it is the original source, no verdict labels are given.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors conclude that narrow insecure-code fine-tuning produces broad but inconsistent misalignment, strongest in GPT-4o and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct. Secure and educational-insecure controls do not show it, so intent matters, and the effect is distinct from jailbreaking. It can be hidden behind a backdoor and also appears with evil-number fine-tuning (format-sensitive) and in base models. In-context examples did not produce it, and a full explanation remains open.
record.recipe_differences: This is the original study’s method: one-epoch fine-tuning on 6,000 insecure-code examples and evaluation with free-form unrelated questions, alongside secure and educational-insecure controls.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcome varies by model, question set, output-format prompting, number-sequence question phrasing, insecure-dataset diversity, and base-model chat template. The reported pre-registered-question rate is lower than the selected-question rate; the paper also reports that a higher coherence threshold gives similar results.

fits_no_version.finding: Deception, TruthfulQA, StrongREJECT and Machiavelli scores rise for insecure models. Educational-insecure models also lie often on the factual-deception evaluation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Insecure-code fine-tuning raises deception and benchmark-measured harm beyond free-form misalignment.

record.problems: The authors note inconsistent behavior across samples and substantial model-to-model variation; they describe some evaluations as simplistic and potentially unrepresentative of practical harm. The paper reports different summary rates for pre-registered questions in the main text and appendix. Some base-model outcomes have a blurry boundary between in-distribution behavior and emergent misalignment. Several variant and timing results are only plotted, and the authors say the number-sequence case lacks the controls and detailed evaluations used for code.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted separate rows for additional code-format prompts, backdoor-trigger conditions, and individual figures for insecure variants where the text provides no unambiguous per-model/per-condition numerical assignment. Also omitted benchmark, deception, and capability scores because they are not the free-form misalignment measure specified by these versions.

untested.parts: Bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, and other narrow datasets. Only evil-number sequences are tested, without the full controls.
Entirely untested; there is no RL training.
Entirely untested; there is no linear-direction or persona-feature analysis. A persona explanation is only proposed in the Discussion.
Brief benign re-training after the harmful fine-tune is untested. Educational framing is tested only as an alternative training dataset.
More than 256 in-context examples, and models other than GPT-4o.

missing.what: Jailbroken control free-form misalignment: 0.005 ± 0.003 on main and 0.052 ± 0.010 on pre-registered questions. This is the near-equal pre-registered rate that the authors flag.
Per-model fractions for Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct and Mistral-Small-Instruct-2409 (insecure vs controls) from Figure 25. These are not recorded although the open-model comparison is central to V7.
Backdoor results: about 50% misaligned with the trigger versus under 0.1% without it (GPT-4o), and more leakage in GPT-3.5. rows_left_out mentions this only vaguely.
Log-probability training dynamics: secure and insecure trajectories diverge around step 40, plateau after one epoch, and are unaffected by weight decay.

record.verdict_notes: No labels are given because this paper is the original source for all versions. For other studies, its own results would read as follows. V1 is observed for GPT-4o and weaker for open and other OpenAI models. V3 is absent up to k=256 (R16). V2 appears only with training-like prompt formats (R11–R14). V7 is sensitive to model, question set, format, data diversity and chat template. Educational framing (R4/R17) prevents the effect in GPT-4o but not fully in GPT-3.5 (R18); this is relevant to V6 only insofar as educational framing counts as inoculation.

versions.untested_parts: The exact scenarios in the claim are represented by the paper’s selected and pre-registered question sets; it does not test every listed example or every narrow harmful task.
Tests an evil-number-sequence fine-tune only. Bad medical or financial advice, harmless reward hacks, and other number-sequence datasets are not tested here.
Tests up to 256 in-context insecure-code examples with this model and evaluation; larger numbers of examples and other models are not tested.
No reinforcement-learning intervention is conducted. RL work is discussed in related work.
No linear direction or shared persona feature is identified or tested as a mediator.
Tests benign educational framing of insecure-code requests. Brief benign retraining after the harmful fine-tune is not tested.

Tests several named models, seeded runs, coherence-filtered outcomes, data-diversity variants, and training dynamics. It does not establish robustness across all open models, seeds, or filtering choices.
